key_insight: Retention-constrained fine-tuning improves an aluminium MACE potential’s defect predictions while preserving its tested near-equilibrium mechanical and vibrational response.
engineering_relevance: The protocol supports more reliable atomistic simulations of aluminium defect dynamics and plasticity without sacrificing validated bulk behavior.
method: Select configurations using force uncertainty from sensitivities over 144 readout weights, updating covariance within each batch.
Iteratively update all model parameters while anchoring historical relative energies.
Gate model acceptance against historical elastic-group energy and vibrational tolerances.
evidence_signal: After 32 acquisitions and 400 gradient updates, mean development force error fell from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Å, outperforming sampling baselines; all three force-uncertainty runs met retention criteria, with harmonic phonon RMS drift below 0.05 THz.
watch_item: Retention is demonstrated only for the tested aluminium configurations and tolerances; broader deployment requires additional validation.
paper_title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
